title: The salted join that loses teams
prompt: Most requests hit `catalog-api`, so this join of requests to their owning team is salted. But some requests come back with no team although their service has an owner. Fix `solve(api_requests)` so it returns `request_id`, `service` and `team` for every request.
rules: Every request appears exactly once, with the team that owns its service in `OWNERS`.
`team` is missing only when the service isn't in `OWNERS` or isn't recorded.
Return only these three columns, in this order.
hints: Look at the salts that the requests get, and the salts that the owner copies get. Do they cover the same numbers?
`F.pmod(..., F.lit(4))` makes salts 0 to 3. How many copies of each owner does `spark.range(3)` make?
Every salt a request can have needs a matching owner copy. Keep the left join, so requests with no owner stay.
explanation: The requests get salts 0 to 3 from `F.pmod(F.hash("request_id"), F.lit(4))`, but `spark.range(3)` copies each owner only for salts 0, 1 and 2. A request with salt 3 finds no owner copy, and the left join keeps it with a missing team. Copy the owners once per salt the requests can have: `spark.range(4)`. (Salting the requests by 3 instead also works: what matters is that the two sides use the same salt values.) Switching to an inner join hides the bug by dropping those requests, and joining on `service` alone matches every copy, so each request comes back several times. The check from the lesson catches all of these: a salted join must return exactly the rows of the plain join.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

OWNERS = [
    ("catalog-api", "catalog"),
    ("checkout-api", "payments"),
    ("auth-service", "identity"),
    ("search-api", "search"),
    ("iot-gateway", "devices"),
]


def solve(api_requests):
    owners = spark.createDataFrame(OWNERS, "service string, team string")
    salts = spark.range(3).select(F.col("id").alias("salt"))
    owners_salted = owners.crossJoin(salts)
    requests_salted = api_requests.select("request_id", "service", F.pmod(F.hash("request_id"), F.lit(4)).alias("salt"))
    joined = requests_salted.join(owners_salted, ["service", "salt"], "left")
    return joined.select("request_id", "service", "team")
